newsitem.title: GERMANY: German rail chief says Transrapid needed.
newsitem.headline: German rail chief says Transrapid needed.

text.p: The head of Deutsche Bahn AG on Sunday said the German railway was in favour of operating the futuristic high-speed Transrapid train that is up for final decision in Bonn in the coming weeks.
"I would welcome it if the Transrapid were to come and we, the railway, would operate it," railway chief Heinz Duerr told German radio.

The federal government, after earlier approving in principal a plan to build a Trasrapid route between Hamburg and Berlin that will cost some nine billion marks, is now set to give final approval for the government part of the financing.

But Bonn's intention to provide nearly six billion marks in financing the construction of the Transrapid track has come under intense criticism by opposition parties and environmental groups who say the huge costs do not justify the project.

Industry officials have stressed, however, that if Germany is to maintain its technological lead in development of the magnetic-levitation technology that drives the train at speeds of over 400 km it must have a proven track record in operation.
"The Transrapid will hardly have a big chance in Europe," said Duerr.

"It will have a chance in populated areas such as Asia and South and North America if they can see the economic and ecological advantages. But only if German industry will build it and can show that it is up and running somewhere," he added.
Under current planning, construction is due to start in 1998, and operations begin in 2005.
The government has said it will cover the costs of the Hamburg-Berlin track, while the private-sector partners develop and operate the train.
The industry partners are led by Thyssen AG, and include Siemens AG, ADtranz, Hochtief AG, Philipp Holzmann AG, Bilfinger & Berger Bau AG and Deutsche Bahn AG.
